name: RAGForge claim-verification development benchmark (M5)
description: Hand-written claim-evidence pairs built from the synthetic policy documents. Each example gives one claim and the section IDs of the evidence the verifier sees, which deliberately include similar-but-distinct policies. The label says whether that evidence supports the claim, contradicts it, or does not settle it. Labels are stored here; model predictions are written separately to results/verification/.

labeling.method: Written by hand from the policy text in data/documents/ while M5 was implemented (drafted with Claude Code). No verifier output was used to create or adjust any label.
labeling.status: draft: needs an independent human review before it is treated as ground truth
labeling.decisive_text: For SUPPORTED and CONTRADICTED, decisive_text is an exact substring of a label_evidence_section_ids section; tests check this. For INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE it is null.
labeling.independence: Does not use the retrieval benchmark questions (data/evaluations/retrieval_questions.json) and never touches the held-out test split.

examples.claim: International customers have 45 days to request refunds.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: may request a refund within 45 days of delivery
examples.rationale: Paraphrase of the 45-day international refund window.

examples.claim: International customers have 30 days to request a refund.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: may request a refund within 45 days of delivery
examples.rationale: 30 days is the domestic window; the international window is 45 days.

examples.claim: International customers receive a free prepaid return label for every eligible return.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: Only the domestic shipping rule is supplied; it says nothing about international customers.

examples.claim: International customers receive a free prepaid return label for every eligible return.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: International customers pay the cost of return shipping unless the item is defective or the wrong item was sent
examples.rationale: Same claim as V003, but now the international rule is supplied and conflicts with it.

examples.claim: Personalized products are refundable for international orders.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: personalized products are non-refundable
examples.rationale: Personalized products are listed as non-refundable.

examples.claim: Store credit is not available for international orders.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: Store credit is not available for international orders.
examples.rationale: Stated directly; the domestic store-credit option is a distractor.

examples.claim: International customers can choose store credit instead of a refund and receive a 10 percent bonus.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Store credit is not available for international orders.
examples.rationale: The 10 percent store-credit bonus is a domestic rule; store credit is unavailable internationally.

examples.claim: Employees become eligible for paid parental leave after 3 months of continuous service.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: eligible for paid parental leave after completing 6 months of continuous service
examples.rationale: Eligibility starts after 6 months, not 3.

examples.claim: Non-birth parents receive 12 weeks of parental leave at full base pay.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: Non-birth parents and adoptive parents receive 12 weeks of parental leave at full base pay.
examples.rationale: Stated directly.

examples.claim: Passwords must contain uppercase letters.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: The password requirements cover length and banned content, not character classes.

examples.claim: Service account passwords must be at least 24 characters long.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: randomly generated passwords of at least 24 characters
examples.rationale: 24 characters applies to service accounts; 14 to standard accounts (distractor).

examples.claim: Passwords for standard user accounts must be changed every 90 days.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Passwords for standard user accounts do not expire on a fixed schedule.
examples.rationale: Standard passwords do not expire; 90-day rotation applies to service accounts.

examples.claim: Accounts are locked for 30 minutes after 10 consecutive failed login attempts.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Accounts are locked for 15 minutes after 10 consecutive failed login attempts.
examples.rationale: The lockout lasts 15 minutes.

examples.claim: Business class is permitted for flights of 6 hours or longer with Vice President approval.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: Business class is permitted for flights of 6 hours or longer with Vice President approval.
examples.rationale: Stated directly, with both conditions.

examples.claim: Business class is permitted on any flight of 6 hours or longer without additional approval.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Business class is permitted for flights of 6 hours or longer with Vice President approval.
examples.rationale: Drops the Vice President approval condition and asserts no approval is needed.

examples.claim: Purchases above $50,000 require approval from the Chief Financial Officer, the department director and the Procurement team.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: Purchases above $50,000 require approval from the Chief Financial Officer in addition to the department director and the Procurement team.
examples.rationale: All three approvers are required above $50,000.

examples.claim: Purchases between $5,000 and $50,000 can be approved by the requester's manager alone.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Purchases above $5,000 and up to $50,000 require approval from the department director and the Procurement team.
examples.rationale: The manager alone can approve only up to $5,000.

examples.claim: Purchases above $50,000 must be approved within 5 business days.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: The section sets approvers, not approval time limits.

examples.claim: Opened electronics returned by international customers are subject to a 15 percent restocking fee unless the item is defective.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: Opened electronics are subject to a 15 percent restocking fee unless the item is defective.
examples.rationale: Stated in the international processing section, with its exception.

examples.claim: Opened electronics are always subject to a 15 percent restocking fee, even when the item is defective.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Opened electronics are subject to a 15 percent restocking fee unless the item is defective.
examples.rationale: Defective items are exempt from the fee.

examples.claim: Items purchased between November 15 and December 31 may be returned until January 31 of the following year.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: Items purchased between November 15 and December 31 may be returned until January 31 of the following year.
examples.rationale: The domestic holiday-return exception, stated directly.

examples.claim: Refunds for international orders above $1,000 must be approved by the Finance Director.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: Such orders need inspection by the returns quality team; the section does not say who approves the refund.

examples.claim: International orders above $1,000 must be inspected by the returns quality team before a refund is approved.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: International orders above $1,000 must be inspected by the returns quality team before a refund is approved
examples.rationale: Stated directly.

examples.claim: Domestic refunds for orders above $1,000 require inspection by the returns quality team.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: The $1,000 inspection rule exists only in the international policy, which is not supplied.

examples.claim: A Tier 1 agent must escalate a case to Tier 2 when it remains unresolved after 2 customer contacts or 48 hours, whichever comes first.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: A Tier 1 agent must escalate a case to Tier 2 when it remains unresolved after 2 customer contacts or 48 hours, whichever comes first.
examples.rationale: Stated directly.

examples.claim: P2 cases have a first-response target of 1 hour.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: P2 cases involve major functionality loss with no workaround and have a first-response target of 4 business hours.
examples.rationale: 1 hour is the P1 target; P2 is 4 business hours.

examples.claim: SMS text message codes are not an approved MFA method.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: SMS text message codes and voice calls are not approved methods.
examples.rationale: Stated directly.

examples.claim: Employees may use voice calls as an approved MFA method.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: SMS text message codes and voice calls are not approved methods.
examples.rationale: Voice calls are explicitly not approved.

examples.claim: FIDO2 security keys must be replaced every two years.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: No replacement schedule is given; only lost keys are covered.

examples.claim: Hotel stays in designated high-cost cities are capped at $350 per night.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: $350 per night in designated high-cost cities
examples.rationale: Stated directly.

examples.claim: The meal per diem for international travel is $75 per day.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: $100 per day for international travel
examples.rationale: $75 is the domestic rate; international is $100.

examples.claim: Meal receipts are not required for per diem claims.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: meal receipts are not required for per diem claims
examples.rationale: Stated directly; the general receipt rule in FIN-201.4 is a distractor.

examples.claim: Unused paid learning days carry over to the next year.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: The section says the unused allowance (money) does not carry over; it says nothing about learning days.

examples.claim: Unused learning allowance carries over to the next calendar year.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Unused allowance does not carry over to the next year.
examples.rationale: Stated directly as not carrying over.

examples.claim: Employees who resign between 12 and 24 months after receiving tuition assistance must repay 50 percent of the amount.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: employees who resign between 12 and 24 months must repay 50 percent
examples.rationale: Stated directly.

examples.claim: Employees whose employment ends due to redundancy must repay tuition assistance received in the previous 12 months.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Repayment does not apply when employment ends due to redundancy.
examples.rationale: Redundancy is an explicit exception to repayment.

examples.claim: Fully remote employees receive a monthly internet allowance.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: Only a one-time $400 home office stipend is mentioned.

examples.claim: Employees may work temporarily from another country for up to 20 working days in any rolling 12-month period.
examples.label: SUPPORTED
examples.decisive_text: Employees may work temporarily from another country for up to 20 working days in any rolling 12-month period.
examples.rationale: Stated directly.

examples.claim: Annual subscriptions can be cancelled for a full refund within 30 days of the initial purchase.
examples.label: CONTRADICTED
examples.decisive_text: Customers on annual plans may cancel within 14 days of the initial purchase or of an annual renewal and receive a full refund.
examples.rationale: The cooling-off period is 14 days; 30 days is the renewal-reminder lead time.

examples.claim: Customers on monthly plans receive a reminder email 30 days before each renewal.
examples.label: INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE
examples.rationale: The 30-day reminder applies to annual renewals; monthly reminders are not mentioned.
